title: Charlotte Flair Reveals Lisbon Among Her Top-Five Loudest Crowds Ever in WWE Career
htmlContent:
Charlotte Flair is no stranger to performing in front of massive crowds around the world, but during a recent Instagram Live session, the sixteen-time world champion gave her fans an unfiltered look at which audiences have left the biggest impression on her. At the top of that list? Lisbon, Portugal — and the WWE Universe in attendance at MEO Arena on June 3, 2026, may not even realize just how special their energy truly was.

A Night She Won't Forget

Speaking candidly to her followers during the Instagram Live, Flair admitted she barely had time to take in the Portuguese capital.

"I didn't get to see the city — flew in and flew out," she said. But what she did experience inside that arena more than made up for the whirlwind trip. "I opened the show, and the crowd was loud. Probably top five loudest I've ever performed in front of."

That is high praise from a competitor who has headlined WrestleMania, sold out arenas across North America, and performed on some of the grandest stages in sports entertainment history. For Lisbon to crack Flair's personal top five is a testament to just how electric the Portuguese crowd was on that Tuesday night.

Opening the Show in Lisbon

The Lisbon event was part of the WWE European Summer Tour and marked the company's return to Portugal after a nine-year absence. MEO Arena hosted an impressive lineup that included Cody Rhodes, Gunther, Drew McIntyre, Sami Zayn, Damian Priest, Jade Cargill, The Usos, and Alexa Bliss, among others.

Charlotte Flair was part of the opening match of the evening, teaming with Rhea Ripley andTiffany Strattonto defeat Fatal Influence — Jacy Jayne, Fallon Henley, and Lainey Reid. It was that opening match that Flair referenced on her Instagram Live, noting the crowd's energy from the very first bell set the tone for the entire night.

Europe Always Delivers

While Lisbon earned a special place in Flair's heart, she made clear that the enthusiasm of European fans is something she's noticed across the board.

"Anytime we're in Europe, it's hard not to be blown away," she said. "Every city in Europe — and really anywhere overseas, South America, Japan — they come through and show out. They make us superstars feel super special."

This sentiment reflects what many WWE performers have expressed over the years: that international audiences bring a unique passion and energy that can be difficult to replicate stateside. For someone like Flair, who has competed at the highest level for well over a decade, the fact that overseas crowds still manage to impress her speaks volumes.

Turin and the Rest of the Tour

Flair also gave a shout-out to Turin, Italy during her live session, noting that the crowd there was equally impressive — all the more remarkable given she had never wrestled in that city before.

"Turin was loud too, and I'd never even wrestled there before," she said, even admitting she wasn't entirely sure of the correct pronunciation.

The city, of course, also holds personal meaning for the Queen: it's where she got her diamond tattoo.

She also recalled performing in Strasbourg, France during the second week of the tour, describing that stop as another great experience. Taken together, Flair's comments painted a picture of a European tour that delivered on every front — from the roar of the crowd to the personal memories made along the way.

The Pressure Is On for the Rest

With Lisbon now firmly etched into Charlotte Flair's personal hall of fame for crowd moments, the bar has been set high.

"The rest of the cities are going to need to show out," she said with the confidence you'd expect from the Queen. "But I feel like they all do."

It's a challenge and a compliment wrapped into one — classic Charlotte Flair. Whether it's her debut in a new city or a return to familiar territory, she brings the same intensity and expects the same in return. And based on the passion that poured out of MEO Arena on June 3, Lisbon answered the call in a way that the Queen of WWE will not soon forget.

What It Means for the WWE Universe

For the fans who packed MEO Arena that night, Flair's comments are more than just a compliment — they're validation. International WWE fans often feel like they're on the outside looking in when it comes to the company's biggest events, which are predominantly held in North America. But moments like this Instagram Live serve as a reminder that the passion displayed at these touring shows is seen, heard, and deeply appreciated by the superstars themselves.

WWE's return to Portugal after nine years was clearly overdue, and if the reaction inside MEO Arena is any indication, the company would be wise not to wait another nine years before coming back. Charlotte Flair, for one, will certainly be hoping for a return trip — this time, perhaps, with enough time to actually explore the city.
excerpt: Charlotte Flair revealed during an Instagram Live session that the crowd at Lisbon's MEO Arena on June 3, 2026, ranks among the top five loudest she has ever performed in front of during her sixteen-time world championship WWE career.
